_README: Golden set for the context-keeper retrieval eval. Run with evals/run_retrieval_eval.py.
AUTHORING RULE, and the main threat to this whole exercise: every question is
written from the PROBLEM the entry solves -- the symptom you would be staring at
before you knew the entry existed -- never by paraphrasing its summary. A query
derived from the summary shares surface tokens with the entry it is supposed to
find, so lexical scoring hits it for free and recall comes out inflated. The
questions below are phrased the way someone would ask BEFORE they knew the answer,
which is the only condition under which the number means anything.
positive  - a real question; `expected` lists every entry that should come back.
negative  - a plausible IN-DOMAIN question with no correct entry. `expected` is
empty. Measures false positives: does retrieval invent an answer?
history   - the correct answer is a SUPERSEDED entry, so this checks that history
stays reachable when you ask for it. Runs against evals/fixtures/
(real content, synthesized supersedes edges) because no live store on
this machine has a single superseded entry -- see build_history_fixtures.py.
`store` is a repo-relative directory name; fixtures are prefixed 'fixtures/'.

STORES ARE PUBLIC-ONLY. A case's `query` and `notes` paraphrase the entry they target, and this repo is public, so cases may only be drawn from stores whose project repo is also public. Cases sourced from private or remote-less projects were removed for this reason and must not be added back (con-015-12da). tests/test_retrieval_eval.py enforces the allowed store list.

cases.query: my agent keeps saying it will write things down later and then the session ends and nothing got recorded
cases.notes: Problem-side: capture batched 'for later' under load. Summary says 'anchored to git commits'.

cases.notes: Corrupt-read-as-empty-store then append. No shared vocabulary with 'atomic write'.

cases.notes: The delivery-timing problem behind scoped re-injection.
